newsitem.title: UK: European bourses mixed, uncertain of new direction.
newsitem.headline: European bourses mixed, uncertain of new direction.

text.p: The main European bourses were mixed-to-higher in thin trading on Monday, pondering whether the bull run in world markets was over after Friday's near 60-point setback on Wall Street.

On the currency front, the dollar edged higher in the European morning but, although sentiment was firm, dealers said it was expected to trade in a narrow range off its overnight peaks against the mark and yen.

In London, Europe's busiest stock exchange, shares traded mixed as investors fretted that Wall Street could be on the verge of a more substantial downside correction after Friday's change of mood in New York.
Early trading volume was light with many awaiting the Dow's open later in the afternoon for a clue to whether Friday was just a blip, or the beginning of a global slide.
"There hasn't been a lot of selling but marketmakers are on their guard," the head of trading at a large brokerage said.
"People are talking about Wall Street coming off several hundred points and don't want to be around if that happens."
The blue chip FTSE 100 has some support at around the 4,200 level and a move below that area could attract some near-term buying, dealers said.
"If we fall much below, institutions will be tempted to buy on the dips," one dealer said. "But if Wall Street has another bad day, the FTSE could head a lot lower."
The FTSE index was down 3.7 at 4215.1 at 1000 GMT

Meanwhile, figures released on Monday showed Britain's economy grew 0.8 percent in the fourth quarter for annual growth of 2.6 percent in 1996. The statistics, which were in line with analysts' expectations, could have a key role in official discussions on whether Britain needs to raise interest rates again.

In Frankfurt, German shares were also mixed in pre-bourse electronic business and bourse trade opened lower with some dealers saying they saw the threat of a decline as the session proceeded. However the firm dollar, which is good for German exports, was providing some support.

In Paris, French stocks were slightly higher on the back of the firmer dollar on the first day of the February account, one boost came from Rhone-Poulenc, which jumped after its unit Rhone-Poulenc Rorer reported good 1996 results.

Foreign exchange dealers said the market was loath to push the dollar much higher before key U.S. data due later this week and amid fears of central bank intervention on a rise above 120 yen. By 1000 GMT the dollar was holding at around 119.16 yen.

Against the mark, Bankers Trust European economist Ernesto Ramirez said: "It looks like the dollar has firm support at around 1.63 marks, and it seems to have the momentum to carry it to 1.6370, maybe looking at 1.64,".

"Today, we're more likely to see consolidation more than anything else...with bias certainly to the positive side, as economic fundamentals continue to support a somewhat stronger dollar," said IBJ International chief analyst Keith Edmonds.

U.S. employment cost data, due on Tuesday, was the focus for now, analysts said, as the results could provide some clues on the Federal Open Market Committee's (FOMC) decision on interest rates at its next meeting on February 4 and 5.
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT
The dollar was at 119.16 yen and 1.6358 marks compared with late Europe's Friday level of 118.93 yen and 1.6265 marks.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1000 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was down 3.7 4215.1
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 4.05 at 2434.39.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was flat at 2998.1
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold in Zurich was trading at around $353.25 compared with its Friday London close of $353.35 an ounce.
